rules.title: Campaign points
rules.text: Mark a box for every Campaign Point the warband gets, as you would mark experience. Whenever the warband reaches a thick-bordered box, read its ambition's achievements to see what it has gained. The marked boxes are at 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 35 and 40; there is no step at 30.

rules.title: Choosing an ambition
rules.text:
Each warband picks one ambition at the beginning of the campaign, from those its warband type may follow, and works towards it throughout the campaign. Every player may always see what every other player has picked.

It does not matter which warband types take part and no player need fight for the side of good: the campaign works with every warband infighting, every one working evil, or every one upholding law and order.

rules.title: Changing ambition
rules.text: A warband may switch to another ambition it is allowed to follow between battles. It loses D6 Campaign Points for doing so.

rules.title: Campaign points once lost
rules.text: Losing Campaign Points never takes back an achievement the warband has already reached. Lost points must still be earned again before the warband can reach its next achievement.

rules.title: Winning the campaign
rules.text: A warband wins as soon as it completes its ambition. An ambition is complete when every box on its Campaign Point track is filled and whatever else its 40-point achievement asks for has been done.

rules.title: Starting over
rules.text: A player who disbands his warband loses its progress and achievements along with its warriors. He picks an ambition for the new warband as if the campaign were beginning. To make up the lost time, the new warband starts with Campaign Points equal to the next lowest amount among the other warbands in the campaign, less D3. The book's own worked example takes the lowest of them instead: the others hold 12, 8 and 9 Campaign Points, a D3 scores 2, and the new warband starts with 8 - 2 = 6.

rules.title: Going insane
rules.text:
A hero's Insanity Points are marked on the normal experience track, but in reverse, so a fighter starts as normal and it takes a long time for the madness to set in. Use a second colour of pencil for them.

A point is marked as soon as it is earned during the game, not after the battle. Whenever a new level is reached the fighter must take a Leadership test at once. On a pass he thinks through the horror and keeps control of himself. On a fail, roll first on the Temporary Insanity chart for how long the insanity lasts and then on the Insanity chart for what it is.

A fighter who fills the track is too insane to continue and must retire.

rules.title: Gaining insanity points
rules.text:
+1 Failing a fear test.
+1 Getting a critical wound.
+1 Being wounded by a poisoned weapon.
+1 Taking drugs.
+D3 Getting the Madness result on the serious injury chart, instead of the normal result.
+1 Getting the Nervous Condition result on the serious injury chart, instead of the normal result.

rules.title: Too insane to care
rules.text:
Many societies and races cannot be twisted any further, being either wholly insane already or finding the terrors somehow acceptable. The insanity rules do not apply at all to henchmen, hired swords, dramatis personae or warriors immune to psychology.

Warriors from Skaven or Troll warbands, warriors immune to fear and warriors suffering from stupidity gain insanity points at half rate: one box is marked for every two points the model gets.

rules.title: A visit to the apothecary
rules.text:
Instead of having a hero search for a rare item in the post-battle sequence you may send him to a physician. Even a warrior who went out of action in the last battle may go, being quite possibly in urgent need of it.

Only one wound, condition or mutation may be treated at a time, and a hero may make only one attempt at treatment in each post-battle sequence. Treatment costs 20 gold crowns, or 50 gold crowns to see a specialist, and must be paid before the roll, because every physician demands payment in advance while the patient is still able to give it.

Each treatment gives one roll on the Limb Surgery chart for an affected body part, or on the Brain Surgery chart for a mental condition. A specialist lets you re-roll the 2D6 once, but the second result stands even if it is worse.

rules.title: Mutation surgery
rules.text:
Treating a mutant does not differ much from the apothecary's usual work, but success may mean something different. Only these mutations can be treated:

Atrophied Arm/Leg, Great Claw, Tentacle, Warped Locomotion. Roll on the Limb Surgery chart, but treat any roll of 9+ as "This has got to come off".
Extra Arm, Poisonous Fangs, Scorpion Tail, Spiked Tail, Spines, Suckers, Supplemental Leg, Warty skin. Roll on the Limb Surgery chart, but treat any roll of 4 as "Sorry lad. Done my best".
Atrophied Head, Daemon Soul, Moronic. Roll on the Brain Surgery chart as normal.

If the warrior bears no other taints once the surgery has succeeded, he is no longer a mutant.

rules.title: Amputations
rules.text:
A warrior may lose one or more limbs to injuries or to successful surgery.

One arm lost: he cannot use a weapon with that arm any more, and may not use two-handed weapons unless he has an extra arm.
All arms lost: he cannot use weapons with his arms at all and every attack counts as unarmed, unless he has a bite attack or a tail. He is also at -3 on all climbing tests.
One leg lost: halve the warrior's Movement, rounding up.
All legs lost: he always counts as knocked down and may not stand up, unless he has a clockwork prosthesis and uses an orichalcum token before the game.

rules.title: Gifted servants
rules.text: Mutation is a sign of favour to the servants of Chaos. Whenever an advance roll gives a hero or hired sword of a Cult of the Possessed, Carnival of Chaos, Beastmen Raiders, Norse or Marauders of Chaos warband a new skill, the warrior may roll on the Stygian Mutation chart instead. On an advance roll of 2 or 12 he is forced to roll on it.

rules.title: Abominations
rules.text:
All players make advance rolls straight after the battle as usual. A hero who rolls a 2 or a 12 on an advance roll has been mutated by the corrupting influence of the Sealed City: instead of choosing a new skill he rolls on the Stygian Mutation chart.

A member of a zealous warband such as Witch Hunters or Maidens of Dusk and Dawn who receives a mutation is purged of the taint by his own brethren with sword and flame. Remove the hero from the roster; his equipment is lost.

The Brood of Ghurash, Skaven and warbands with the Fear the Abyss ambition revere all things twisted and suffer no penalty for being a mutant.

Any other warband's hero can usually expect to be cast out by his suspicious peers once word gets around. Before the start of the next battle take a Leadership test using the warband leader's characteristic, at +1 for each mutant the warband is already harbouring and +1 for each time the leader has had to roll on the Insanity chart. If the test is passed the mutant is put to death: strike him from the roster and discard his equipment. If it is failed the shamed warrior is allowed to remain with the warband, and no further test is needed unless he receives another mutation. No test is needed if the mutant has successfully undergone surgery at the apothecary in the post-battle sequence. The test is failed automatically if the leader himself becomes a mutant or already is one.

rules.title: Using the new weapons
rules.text: Unless a weapon introduced in the Sealed City is on his warband's equipment list, only a model with the Weapons Training skill may ever use it.

battle_rules.title: Multiple weapons
battle_rules.text: Every mutation that can be used in close combat has a weapon profile, so a mutant may end up with three or more usable melee weapons. He gains one extra attack with the weapon's profile for each weapon beyond the first, not just for the second. A warrior with a sword, a great claw and a sharp beak could make all his profile attacks with the great claw and an extra attack with each of the other two.

battle_rules.title: Clockwork ammunition
battle_rules.text: Clockwork weapons may use special types of ammunition, which are used up for a single battle. Declare in each shooting phase which ammunition the warrior will use before choosing a target.

charts.title: Temporary Insanity
charts.description: Rolled first when a fighter fails the Leadership test at a new insanity level: how long the insanity lasts.

rows.text: D6 turns. Treat as 2-3 if the madness occurs during the exploration phase.
The next battle.
Next two battles.
Indefinite.

charts.title: Insanity
charts.description: Rolled after the Temporary Insanity chart: the type of insanity the fighter gets.
charts.note: All results are unique: a result rolled twice is rolled again until a new type of insanity comes up. Unless a result says otherwise, it lasts as long as was rolled on the Temporary Insanity chart.

rows.name: Catatonia
rows.text: The fighter falls to the floor and rolls into the fetal position. Treat as stupidity where the fighter has automatically failed his Leadership test.

rows.name: Amnesia
rows.text: The warrior forgets D3 random skills or spells.

chart.title: Panzaism or Quixotism
chart.description: Which of the two the fighter is taken by.

rows.name: Panzaism
rows.text: The warrior is immune to fear and The Terror, as he sees all things, even supernatural ones, as ordinary.

rows.name: Quixotism
rows.text: The fighter sees everything and everyone as supernatural threats. He must pass a Leadership test at the beginning of the movement phase or become frenzied while in hand-to-hand combat, or charge the closest model or piece of terrain bigger than him, which rules out rocks and barrels. He has to attack his foe until he takes him out of action or passes the Leadership test, which lets him break free from combat automatically (see LRB Optional Rules).

rows.name: Paranoia
rows.text: The fighter is always on edge and thinks someone is out to get him. He may not run but may charge into combat as normal. He always strikes first in combat unless he is carrying a double-handed weapon.

rows.name: Phobia
rows.text: The fighter is cursed with a permanent or temporary phobia. Causing fear does not stop a model from taking a phobia-induced fear test itself.

chart.title: Phobia
chart.description: Which phobia the fighter is cursed with.

rows.name: Claustrophobia
rows.text: The fighter must pass a Leadership test to enter a building, or each turn to move if he is inside a tunnel or similar.

rows.name: Acrophobia
rows.text: The fighter must take a Leadership test each turn he is on a higher floor or area.

rows.name: Nyctophobia
rows.text: As long as the sight conditions are worse than bright, the fighter has to pass a Leadership test at the beginning of each turn to move.

rows.name: Agoraphobia
rows.text: If he wants to move more than 2" away from a building or wall, he must pass a Leadership test first.

rows.name: Anthrophobia
rows.text: His kin scares the fighter. Enemy models of the same race as the fighter inspire fear in him, while friendly models do not stop him from being all alone.

rows.name: Aichmophopia
rows.text: Fighters armed with a sword, a spear or another weapon with a sharp or pointy end inspire fear in the fighter.

rows.name: Murderous Delirium
rows.text: Something snaps inside the fighter's mind and he gives in to the rage. He does not recognise any model as friendly and becomes frenzied. If he is out of charge range he runs towards the nearest visible model instead.

rows.name: Megalomania
rows.text: The fighter may not hide or end his movement phase behind an obstacle. He is immune to all alone tests. If he is the leader of the warband he cannot make a voluntary rout for as long as this result lasts.

rows.name: Corrupted in Mind and Body
rows.text: The warrior's body reacts to the unnatural changes his mind undergoes. Roll on the Stygian Mutation chart and apply the result permanently at once.

rows.name: Criminal Psychosis
rows.text: The fighter hates everyone.

rows.name: Abyssal Nightmares
rows.text: The fighter has seen too much and is plagued by horrible nightmares. The model misses the next game and must take a Leadership test. On a pass he has defeated the nightmares and loses D3 insanity points; on a fail his fragile mind suffers even more and he gains D6 insanity points. These effects are always permanent, whatever was rolled on the duration chart.

rows.name: Completely Bonkers
rows.text: The fighter may not take part in any battle as long as the insanity endures, his fragile mind no longer bearing the Sealed City's horrors. If the madness is permanent, remove him from your roster instead.

charts.title: Limb Surgery
charts.description: Rolled for a hero treated at the apothecary, once per treatment paid for.
charts.note: The injuries that can be treated are Leg Wound, Smashed Leg and Hand Injury.

rows.name: Someone fetch a priest...
rows.text: The unfortunate patient has expired due to excessive blood loss. The hero is dead and must be stricken from the warband roster, but his equipment is retained by the warband.

rows.name: This has got to come off
rows.text: The surgeon has felt the need to amputate, ostensibly to keep the rot out, and the warrior loses the treated limb or limbs.

rows.name: Sorry lad. Done my best
rows.text: The surgery was unsuccessful, and the warrior must miss the next battle while he recovers.

rows.name: No Luck
rows.text: The surgery was unsuccessful.

rows.name: Mind you stay off it for a bit
rows.text: The surgery was successful! The warrior may remove the injury and its adverse effects from his profile. He must, however, miss the next battle while he recovers.

rows.name: Shallaya be praised!
rows.text: The surgery was a complete success! The warrior may remove the injury and its adverse effects from his profile.

charts.title: Brain Surgery
charts.description: Rolled for a hero treated at the apothecary, once per treatment paid for.
charts.note: The conditions that can be treated are Madness and Nervous Condition.

rows.name: Someone fetch a priest...
rows.text: The physician has been a bit too zealous in his treatment. The hero is dead and must be stricken from the warband roster, but his equipment is retained by the warband.

rows.name: Erm... That's not right
rows.text: The treatment has not only failed to help the warrior, it has actually worsened his condition! The warrior is now subject to stupidity. If the warrior was being treated for stupidity there is no change in his condition, except perhaps a bit more drooling than usual.

rows.name: A bit unhinged, that one
rows.text: The treatment has failed, and the warrior emerges from the procedure as something of a raving lunatic. His Initiative suffers a -1 penalty, down to a minimum of 1, and he is now so unsettling to behold that he causes fear.

rows.name: Sorry lad. Done my best
rows.text: The treatment was unsuccessful, and the warrior must miss the next battle while he recovers.

rows.name: A bit of rest and you'll be fine
rows.text: The treatment was successful! The warrior may remove the injury and its adverse effects from his profile. He must, however, miss the next battle while he recovers.

rows.name: Shallaya be praised!
rows.text: The treatment was a complete success! The warrior may remove the injury and its adverse effects from his profile.

charts.title: Stygian Mutations
charts.description: Rolled when an advance roll of 2 or 12 makes a hero a mutant (Abominations), when a hero or hired sword of a Chaos warband takes a mutation instead of a new skill (Gifted servants), on the Insanity chart's Corrupted in Mind and Body, and wherever a Fear the Abyss achievement says so.
charts.note: A result with no text here is the mutation of that name in Boons & Banes.

rows.name: Moronic
rows.text: The mutant's mind shrivels. The mutant is now subject to stupidity.

rows.name: Emaciated Appearance
rows.text: The mutant becomes a matchstick figure, sickly thin and bony. Divide its Toughness in half, rounding up.

rows.name: Shrink
rows.text: The warrior's body becomes hunched and shrunken. Reduce the mutant's Movement and Initiative by 1.

rows.name: Warty Skin
rows.text: The mutant is covered in repellent warts that make his outward appearance most unpleasant. The warrior is at -1 when rolling to find rare items.

rows.name: Brightly Patterned Skin
rows.text: The mutant's skin becomes brightly coloured with contrasting patterns, making it difficult to hide. Unless the mutant is wearing a cloak, enemy models can spot him using twice their Initiative in inches.

rows.name: Supplemental Leg
rows.text: The mutant grows an additional leg and his Movement is increased by 1. An unnatural number of legs is no base for coordinated movement, so the mutant may no longer run. He still doubles his Movement when charging as normal.

rows.name: Hollow Bones
rows.text: The mutant becomes significantly lighter, but also more fragile, as he develops a bird-like bone structure. The warrior may re-roll failed Initiative tests when jumping and making diving charges, but loses 1 Toughness.

rows.name: Atrophied Leg
rows.text: One of the mutant's legs has become shrivelled and atrophied. Divide the mutant's Movement in half, rounding up.

rows.name: Warped Locomotion
rows.text: The mutant's legs fuse together and thicken until his lower body resembles a maggot or snail. Reduce the mutant's Movement by 2, but ignore any knocked down results he would suffer, as if he had the Jump Up skill.

rows.name: Atrophied Arm
rows.text: One of the mutant's arms has become shrivelled and atrophied. The mutant suffers -1 Weapon Skill and -1 Strength on all attacks made with the arm.

rows.name: Atrophied Head
rows.text: The mutant's head has become shrivelled and atrophied. He loses 1 Initiative and 2 Leadership.

location_groups.name: The Physician
location_groups.description: A physician's surgery: a ramshackle shop in the outpost, a Skaven laboratory or a trollish butcher's cave.

locations.name: The Apothecary
locations.rules:
Instead of searching for a rare item, a Hero may go to a physician, even one who went out of action in the last battle. Only one wound, condition or mutation is treated at a time, and each Hero gets one treatment in each post-battle sequence.

A treatment costs 20 gold crowns, or 50 gold crowns from a specialist, paid before the roll. It gives one roll on the Limb Surgery chart for a Leg Wound, Smashed Leg or Hand Injury, or on the Brain Surgery chart for Madness or a Nervous Condition. A specialist lets you re-roll the 2D6 once, and the second result stands even if it is worse.

A mutant may be treated too, by the Mutation surgery rule: Atrophied Arm/Leg, Great Claw, Tentacle and Warped Locomotion roll on the Limb Surgery chart, treating 9+ as This has got to come off; Extra Arm, Poisonous Fangs, Scorpion Tail, Spiked Tail, Spines, Suckers, Supplemental Leg and Warty skin roll on the Limb Surgery chart, treating 4 as Sorry lad. Done my best; Atrophied Head, Daemon Soul and Moronic roll on the Brain Surgery chart as normal. A warrior with no other taint once the surgery has succeeded is no longer a mutant. A limb lost to surgery follows the Amputations rule.
